title: Local storage and privacy
description: Understand what Quickque stores on a device, what remains temporary, and where local-network and screen-sharing boundaries matter.
body:
# Local storage and privacy

Quickque is designed to keep a personal meeting script close to the device. There is no Quickque account, cloud script library, cloud transcription service, analytics pipeline, or silent online fallback in the current app. Local-first is a boundary to understand, not a promise that every device or network is automatically safe.

## Optional packaged Mac distribution

Quickque's source code and documentation remain available under the [MIT License](https://github.com/rossboyd/quickque/blob/main/LICENSE), and source builds remain available. A proposed packaged Mac distribution is **£77 as a one-time purchase**, separate from those free MIT rights. A purchased version is intended to remain usable forever; future major upgrades may cost extra.

There is no verified release or native Mac validation yet, so live purchases remain gated. A sandbox preview checkout creates no license or download. If checkout is enabled, browser scripts and audio remain local; billing and payment data goes to [Stripe's privacy policy](https://stripe.com/privacy). The website backend processes payment references and guest-checkout verification, not Quickque scripts or audio. See the [Stripe commerce runbook](https://github.com/rossboyd/quickque/blob/main/artifacts/quickque-website/docs/COMMERCE.md) for the current checkout boundary.

## Before you begin

- Decide which browser origin or desktop app you intend to use; their storage is separate.
- Back up scripts before clearing site data, uninstalling, moving scripts to Trash, permanently deleting them, or moving between the browser and Mac app.
- Use the native app only on a Mac and network you trust. Review the [Phone Remote](/guide/phone-remote/) warning about unencrypted local HTTP.

## What persists locally

1. The library envelope in local device storage includes live scripts, the active selection, Trash entries, custom order, and sort mode. Library state is committed together so a failed write does not claim a partial save.

2. Reader and appearance settings such as **Dark Theme**, **Overlay Opacity**, font size, scroll speed, and Compact Overlay preference are stored separately from the library backup.

3. A successful Flow model installation is durably cached under `~/Library/Application Support/Quickque/Flow/` on the Mac. Model files are not included in **Export Full Backup**.

4. Use **Settings & backups** → **Export Full Backup** when you need a portable copy. The version 2 JSON contains scripts, active selection, Trash, custom order, and sort mode, but not settings or Flow models. See [Backup, restore, and migration](/guide/backup-restore/).

## What remains temporary

1. Local Flow captures the selected microphone, never system audio, and processes it in memory. Audio is not written to a recording or sent to a service.

2. Recognition events and transcript text are transient. Quickque does not save, back up, or log transcripts. This is a product storage boundary, not a claim of forensic erasure from every operating-system layer.

3. Document import reads selected bytes in a disposable bundled worker. It makes no upload, does not execute document markup, does not render imported HTML, and does not fetch embedded resources. The review text becomes persistent only when you choose **Save as Script**.

4. Phone Remote exchanges minimal reader state and validated control commands over the local session. It does not serve script text, audio, transcripts, model files, or library contents. The token is kept out of URLs and browser history, but the transport is still HTTP and therefore unencrypted.

## Steps

### Safer meeting steps

1. Use **Settings & backups** → **Export Full Backup** before changing storage, moving scripts to Trash, permanently deleting a script, or uninstalling the app. Store it privately because it contains live and trashed script text.

2. Grant microphone permission only when you intentionally choose **Start microphone** in native Flow. Downloading model files does not request the microphone.

3. If you use Phone Remote, pair only on a trusted reachable LAN, approve the expected phone on the Mac, and stop the session when finished. Do not expose the local HTTP service to a network you do not trust.

4. Choose only the intended application or window when sharing Zoom or Meet. The Mac overlay can appear in screen sharing or recording; it does not modify the meeting camera feed.

5. When moving between browser and desktop, use **Settings & backups** → **Export Full Backup** in the source origin and **Import Backup JSON** in the destination. Existing web storage is not migrated automatically; import adds content and preserves the destination's current selection and sort mode.

## Expected result

Scripts, Trash, sort/order metadata, settings, and deliberately installed models stay on their respective local origins or Mac storage. Audio and recognition text disappear from Quickque's working memory when Flow stops, without becoming app backup data. Import and Phone Remote remain local workflows with the documented network caveat.

## Troubleshooting

- **My browser and desktop have different scripts:** separate localStorage origins are expected. Use **Export Full Backup** and **Import Backup JSON** rather than assuming synchronization.
- **A transcript appears after Flow stops:** the reader may show temporary status or matching text while active; Quickque does not persist transcript events as a recording, backup, or transcript log. Check the app state and report any reproducible persisted file.
- **Phone Remote feels private because it is local:** local does not mean encrypted. HTTP traffic can be observed by someone who can access the network; use a trusted LAN only.
- **A document import seems to need the internet:** it should not fetch document resources or a runtime CDN. Stop and investigate a network request instead of treating it as expected behavior.
- **Screen sharing shows Quickque:** select a specific meeting window or application in the sharing picker. A native always-on-top overlay may be captured when sharing the whole display.
- **I want to clear everything:** export first with **Export Full Backup**. Browser storage, Trash, and desktop storage must be cleared or uninstalled deliberately, and Flow models are separate from JSON backups.

Privacy-sensitive behavior, microphone permission, native packaging, and physical remote behavior still need Mac verification. Read [Requirements and installation](/guide/requirements-installation/) for the current release status.
